import pandas as pd

# List all source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_5/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_5/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_5/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_5/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_5/training_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_5/training_5.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_5/training_6.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_5/training_7.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_5/training_8.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_5/training_9.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_5/training_10.csv"
]

# Read all source CSV files into a list of DataFrames
# Use index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column as per Hint 24
dfs = [pd.read_csv(path, index_col=0) for path in source_files]

# All source tables have the same schema ['code', 'name'] which matches the target schema exactly.
# According to Hint 2 and Hint 4, we should UNION all source tables.

# Concatenate all DataFrames (union)
combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Ensure the data types match the target schema:
# 'code': integer, 'name': string
combined_df['code'] = combined_df['code'].astype(int)
combined_df['name'] = combined_df['name'].astype(str)

# The target examples show duplicates exist (e.g., code=11 repeated multiple times),
# and the target examples have 1374 tuples, so we keep duplicates as is (no deduplication).

# Write the combined DataFrame to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_5/target_multisource_cot.csv"
combined_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
